h.strategy: Use retrieved findings to classify settings as strong, weak, neutral or harmful, and to identify which settings can disconnect other parts from the outcome. Propose hypotheses only of two kinds. Self-conditioning: the edit's effect depends on the value it replaces, being more negative when that value is strong and more positive when it is empty or harmful. Disconnection: when the edited part cannot influence the outcome, its effect shrinks toward zero, so the direction is lower if the edit usually helps and higher if it usually hurts. Directions refer to the signed effect. For each hypothesis, state the edit's usual sign and a one-sentence mechanism. Cover varied edit fields and values. The critic should replace any hypothesis with an uncertain usual sign, competing effects or reliance on partial redundancy.

hyps.why: With edge 0 removed node 1 receives no input, so a conv on edge 4 processes nothing and its usual positive gain vanishes.
Edge 2 reaches the output only through node 2 and edge 5, so with edge 5 removed a 3x3 conv on edge 2 cannot affect the output.
Edge 1 feeds node 2, whose only exit is edge 5, so with edge 5 removed the conv upgrade becomes irrelevant.
With edge 0 removed node 1 carries no signal, so a conv on edge 2 is disconnected and its usual gain shrinks toward zero.
With node 1 cut off from the input by edge 0 being none, a 1x1 conv on edge 4 has nothing to process and the gain disappears.
Upgrading an already strong 1x1 conv on the direct edge to 3x3 gives little gain compared with replacing weaker ops.
Filling an empty direct input-to-output edge with a conv adds a new learnable path and gains more than replacing an existing op.
Edge 5 is the only exit of node 2, so replacing none with a 3x3 conv reconnects that whole branch and gains far more than upgrading an existing op.
Replacing an empty edge 1 with a conv adds a parallel feature path into node 2 and gains more than replacing an existing op.
Edge 0 is the sole input to node 1, so filling it with a conv reactivates the whole node-1 branch and gains more than swapping one existing op for another.
